raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"From Square Jean XXIII, make your way on to Notre-Dame, about a seven-minute walk away.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":6},{"text":"In 1804, Napoleon stood inside these walls and crowned himself emperor — and the walls behind him were so dilapidated they had to be covered with drapes to make a backdrop grand enough for the occasion.","source_id":"6fd66eb3-2ccd-423b-aa6c-d01507a312b7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":6},{"text":"How the great cathedral came to that state is a story worth walking back through, because this is a Gothic masterpiece, rearing up from the Ile de la Cité like a great ship moored by its huge flying buttresses.","source_id":"6fd66eb3-2ccd-423b-aa6c-d01507a312b7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":6},{"text":"Construction began in 1160 under Bishop de Sully and wasn't finished until around 1345, all of it rising over the Merovingian cathedral of St-Etienne — which had itself stood on an old Roman temple to Jupiter.","source_id":"6fd66eb3-2ccd-423b-aa6c-d01507a312b7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":6},{"text":"Its seminaries became an ecclesiastical powerhouse, turning out six popes across the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries, before it slowly lost ground to rival sees like Rheims and St-Denis.","source_id":"6fd66eb3-2ccd-423b-aa6c-d01507a312b7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":6},{"text":"The facade is the cathedral's most impressive feature; the Romanesque influence still shows in its solid H-shape, but what really strikes you is the lightness and grace created by the filigree of the central rose window and the gallery above it.","source_id":"8094c405-a3ea-47cb-91cb-4e791f7f503a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":6},{"text":"By then the building had fallen into decline, and when the Revolution came, enthusiasts mistook the Old Testament kings on the facade for the kings of France and tore them down — so the twenty-seven huge figures beneath the rose window, the biblical ancestors of Christ, are all copies.","source_id":"37e95b17-1dfc-454a-9dbd-0fa8c1d16f5a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":6,"also_cites":["6fd66eb3-2ccd-423b-aa6c-d01507a312b7"]},{"text":"Now drop your eyes to the portals, and to the most arresting carving of all, above the central door: the Day of Judgement, its lower frieze a whirl of the dead climbing from their graves while Christ presides above, sending the souls on his right to heaven and those on his left to hell.","source_id":"cf823873-9a35-44cf-97f5-83b15ec7c674","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":6},{"text":"Look closer at the arch and you'll find alert, mischievous little angels peering out — said to be modelled on the cathedral's own choirboys.","source_id":"cf823873-9a35-44cf-97f5-83b15ec7c674","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":6},{"text":"The left portal shows Mary crowned by Christ with scenes of her life below, and the right shows the Virgin enthroned above episodes from the life of her mother, St Anne, and the life of Christ.","source_id":"ab3aae94-a724-48d2-8a36-573e734d618f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":6},{"text":"They're carved with real cunning — in the nativity, the infant Christ is placed above Mary to mark his higher status, and laid on an altar instead of a crib, a quiet hint at the sacrifice to come.","source_id":"ab3aae94-a724-48d2-8a36-573e734d618f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":6},{"text":"Step through the door and you're standing right beneath the bell tower, so look up at the vault for the trapdoor the bells were hoisted through, and notice the two pillars carrying the towers' whole weight.","source_id":"102ff4b1-b136-4ab6-82f5-717efce836a9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":6},{"text":"They're massive.","source_id":"102ff4b1-b136-4ab6-82f5-717efce836a9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":6},{"text":"For all that history, Notre-Dame still sits at the heart of Paris and, many will tell you, at the symbolic heart of France.","source_id":"d1a26b29-cee0-4fcf-b440-3b9d5f3c5a08","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":6},{"text":"Out on the pavement by the west door, look down for the small marker in the stone — a brass stud, a bronze star, kilometre zero — which people rub as a wishing stone but which is really the Zero Point of Paris, the spot from which every main-road distance in France is measured.","source_id":"301f72bd-8ca8-4e32-b49c-656df75be3d2","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":6,"also_cites":["d1a26b29-cee0-4fcf-b440-3b9d5f3c5a08"]},{"text":"That wide, windswept square you crossed is the Parvis — from the word paradise — laid out by Haussmann in the 1860s, and the white paving blocks set into it trace the little medieval streets and buildings that once crowded this ground.","source_id":"d1a26b29-cee0-4fcf-b440-3b9d5f3c5a08","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":6},{"text":"One last curiosity before we finish: the remains of Abelard and Heloise have had an extraordinary journey through the centuries.","source_id":"7a8f10f0-2ef6-4403-98e6-8e5aa7928f5b","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":6},{"text":"And that brings our walk to a close.","source_id":"GLUE_CLOSING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":6},{"text":"Thank you for coming along with me today, and when you're ready, take your time to keep exploring on your own.","source_id":"GLUE_CLOSING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":6}]}
